title: release-notes: a small made-up skill that writes release notes
name: release-notes

fields.does: writes the release notes for a version from its merged pull requests

fields.when: someone asks for the notes of a version that is tagged, or about to be
a release branch is cut and its notes are missing

fields.what: the change log of a single pull request

fields.situation: a request to sum up a week's commits for a status update

fields.text:
## 2.4.0

### Breaking
- The `--out` flag now needs a file name.

### Added
- Dark mode for the report page.

### Fixed
- Long titles no longer cut off the summary.

fields.good: each line says what changed for the reader, grouped by kind, breaking changes first
fields.so-so: the pull request titles, pasted in merge order

fields.text: reads every pull request merged since the last tag
groups the changes as breaking, added and fixed

fields.what: that every merged pull request carries a label

fields.decision: what counts as a breaking change

fields.when: a breaking change has no line in its pull request
fields.then: lists that pull request and waits for your words

fields.when: the notes are ready to publish

fields.why: the maintainer reads the notes before they go out anyway

fields.capability: read merged pull requests and tags through gh
fields.reason: the notes are written from them
fields.detail: gh pr list --state merged; gh release view

fields.text: it never pushes, tags or publishes on its own

fields.needs: the gh command line, signed in

fields.act: opens a draft release on GitHub
fields.tells-first: the version and the notes it will post
fields.yes: your yes in chat, for that one draft

fields.rule: Never write a change that no pull request names
fields.guards: notes that promise what was not shipped
a pull request merged after the tag slipping into the notes

fields.meaning: a change that makes a user's setup stop working until they act
one tagged version and its notes

fields.text: plain sentences in the past tense, one change per line, no emoji
